note: College mental health, loneliness & leaving home; body image; help-seeking (UNESCO 5.6, 5.5, 6.4). New v2 build, the College wellbeing anchor. Leaving home is exciting and lonely and hard; look after your mind, find your people, and know that asking for help is the strong move. Five modes: settling in (homesickness/loneliness normalised), find your people (belonging is built), cope well (healthy coping ONLY, body image & self-worth), reach out (help=strength, UN&RE), tools & crisis routing. HIGH-CARE: any sign of distress is met with warmth and an immediate route to help, never assessment questions; only healthy coping (no strategy using pain, restriction or shock; nothing reinforcing self-harm); anti-stigma, not therapy; persistent or serious distress is pointed to professionals. Builds on g39 (Bounce), continues g42 (Life Ready); pairs with g48 and g52; underpins every College node. India: academic pressure, hostel isolation, far from home, family expectations, stigma (especially young men); Tele-MANAS 14416 (primary), KIRAN 1800-599-0019, campus counsellors, a trusted person.

evidenceBase: Leaving home for college or work is one of life's hardest transitions and a peak window for mental-health difficulty, so homesickness, loneliness and a bumpy first few months are common and normal, not weakness; they ease as routine and connection grow. Belonging is built rather than found: reaching out first, joining things, saying yes and finding even one or two real connections beats isolation, and almost everyone feels like an outsider at the start (WHO adolescent & young-adult mental health; transition research)

Only healthy coping is taught, never anything using pain, restriction or shock, and nothing that reinforces self-harm: routine, sleep, movement, eating regularly, time outdoors, talking to someone, breathing and grounding, breaks and enjoyable activity all help stress and low mood, while powering through by skipping sleep, food or breaks, numbing, isolating and harsh self-criticism do not. Impostor feelings are common, especially for first-generation students, and don't reflect reality, and self-worth is not a person's grades or appearance (WHO; coping and self-worth research; links Body Confident g21)

Reaching out for help early is the strong, smart move, not failure, and you don't have to be in crisis to deserve support; stigma, especially around young men, is dismantled by normalising help-seeking. Any sign of heavy low mood or thoughts of self-harm is met with warmth and an immediate, concrete route to help, not assessment questions: Tele-MANAS 14416 (India's primary 24/7 line), KIRAN 1800-599-0019, a campus counsellor, or a trusted person. This is anti-stigma skill-building and signposting, never therapy, and persistent or serious distress is pointed to professionals (WHO; India Tele-MANAS / Manodarpan)

Losing interest in everything you loved

scenarios.relearn: Weeks of heavy low mood or losing all interest is a signal to reach for support; a tough afternoon or pre-event nerves are normal.

scenarios.hook: Sam: you don't have to carry any of this alone, ever. Let that land?
scenarios.affirm: You never have to carry it alone; support, in people and helplines, is always within reach.
scenarios.relearn: You don't have to carry any of this alone; support is always within reach.

scenarios.hook: You want to invite a couple of acquaintances to become real friends.

yourLine.text: "I'm getting a few people together this weekend, would you like to come?"
Wait for them to make the first move forever

scenarios.relearn: A simple invitation can turn acquaintances into real friends.

scenarios.hook: You realise you've been coping by drinking more than you'd like.

options.text: Notice it without shame and swap in healthier coping
options.consequence: You catch it early and adjust.

options.text: Tell yourself it's fine, everyone does it
options.consequence: Noticing it kindly and swapping in healthier coping (and support if needed) beats brushing it off.

scenarios.debrief: Numbing with substances is a common but draining coping trap; noticing it early and swapping in healthier strategies, with support if needed, helps.
scenarios.relearn: If you're leaning on substances to cope, notice it kindly and swap in healthier coping.

scenarios.hook: Spot the kind, true thing to tell yourself when it's hard.
scenarios.relearn: It tends to get better; a year on you'll likely feel far more at home.

scene.text: "This is hard now, and it tends to get better"
"A year on, I'll likely feel more at home"

scenarios.why: 'It gets better' and 'more at home in a year' are kind and true; 'always this bad' isn't.

scenarios.hook: You're unsure whether to use a helpline like Tele-MANAS for 'just' stress.

options.text: Use it; it's there for exactly this, no problem too small
options.consequence: You get support without waiting for a crisis.

options.text: Decide you're not 'bad enough' to call
options.consequence: Tele-MANAS 14416 is there for exactly this; no problem is too small, and you don't have to be in crisis.

scenarios.debrief: Helplines like Tele-MANAS are for everyday stress too, not only crises; reaching out is always valid.
scenarios.relearn: Helplines like Tele-MANAS 14416 are for everyday stress too; no problem is too small.

scenarios.hook: "Being kind to yourself is soft or weak."
scenarios.relearn: Being kind to yourself isn't soft; it's how you keep going.

myth.un: Being kind to yourself is soft or weak.
myth.re: Self-kindness isn't soft; it's how you actually keep going.

scenarios.hook: Sort: something this game does, or something it doesn't?

items.text: Builds coping skills and signposts help

scenarios.relearn: This builds skills and signposts help; it doesn't diagnose, treat or replace a professional.

scenarios.hook: Sort: deepens belonging over time, or stays surface?

items.text: Being there for people in hard times

scenarios.relearn: Showing up in hard times and sharing realness deepens belonging; only small talk or arm's length stays surface.

scenarios.hook: Sam: look after your mind, find your people, and ask for help, that's how you thrive, not just survive. Ready?
scenarios.affirm: Carry that, and you can truly thrive here, and help others do the same. You're not alone.
scenarios.relearn: Look after your mind, find your people and ask for help: that's how you thrive.
